subject.title: [Bug]: Codex app-server intermittently produces no model events for 120s, then profile cooldown causes cascading fallbacks

question: Should an accepted Codex app-server turn that produces no model events be treated as an auth-profile failure with cooldown, or as a runtime transport failure that may fall back without penalizing the profile?
rationale: The current generic timeout path couples runtime liveness to persistent profile health, and source inspection alone cannot choose the intended operational policy without risking either repeated dead runtimes or unnecessary account lockout.

options.title: Separate Runtime Failure
options.body: Classify eventless app-server timeouts separately, restart the client and permit fallback without profile cooldown unless provider evidence identifies a profile failure.

options.title: Keep Generic Timeout Cooldown
options.body: Preserve cooldown for all timeout-shaped failures and focus only on diagnosing why Codex stopped emitting events.

options.title: Wait For Upstream Codex
options.body: Treat OpenClaw's current timeout and cooldown behavior as containment while tracking the terminal-event failure entirely upstream.

recommendation.title: Separate Runtime Failure
recommendation.body: Classify eventless app-server timeouts separately, restart the client and permit fallback without profile cooldown unless provider evidence identifies a profile failure.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work covers both Codex app-server liveness and missing-completion recovery, making this the strongest available routing signal for the policy boundary.
